subject: Post-call: OpsAI inference serving architecture and SLO checklist
messages:
From: Claire Sun <claire.sun@opsai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi@opsai.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Oct 2029 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: OpsAI discovery recap — throughput & latency constraints

Markus / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the clear line-up of options. Below is a short recap from our side and the high-level constraints so you can map to an architecture + SLO proposal.

Key pain points we reiterated on the call:
- Tail latency on production spikes: p95 currently ~1.9s (severe user impact for interactive flows).
- Predictable cost per 1k requests — finance needs a tighter cost band for Q1.
- Model parity drift: we run a fine-tuned Llama-3-13B variant in-house and want to keep parity when served by a managed platform.
- Compliance: VPC-only deployment with audit logs and KMS integration is mandatory.

Workload profile (sampled):
- Typical request: ~140 tokens (prompt + response)
- Sustained baseline: 150 RPS during business hours; burst up to 700 RPS for 30–120s during campaigns
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent sessions at peak
- Target user-facing SLOs: p95 end-to-end <= 400ms for short (<=64 token) responses, p50 <= 120ms; relaxed for >512 token generations

Model requirements and constraints:
- Context length: 2048 tokens (some clients may push to 4096 within 2029 roadmap)
- Model: open replica of Llama-3-13B; we plan a light fine-tune layer (adds ~3–4% additional memory needs)
- KV cache reuse is important for multi-turn flows (expect >40% prefix reuse)

Deployment preferences:
- Preference: Private deployment (VPC) with Redwood Private control plane and optional Dedicated during campaign bursts.
- Fallback: Use a 7B-compatible distilled variant for overflow if cost/latency tradeoffs demand it

Attachments: I uploaded a short throughput matrix and our procurement window to the shared Drive (opsai-throughput-matrix.xlsx).

Next asks from OpsAI:
1) Rough capacity/architecture recommendation covering baseline + burst scenario (including expected GPU counts and quantization suggestions)
2) Example latency/cost tradeoffs for 13B vs 7B quantized variants on the same topology
3) SOC2 + audit log sample and KMS integration notes

Happy to set a follow-up demo the week of Oct 14.

—Claire
Claire Sun
Head of Platform
OpsAI

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Sun <claire.sun@opsai.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Oct 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OpsAI discovery recap — throughput & latency constraints

Claire — thanks for the succinct summary and the matrix. I captured the ask and sketched a recommended topology and SLO plan below; pinging Irene and Grace for technical validation and action items.

High-level recommendation (baseline + burst):
- Private deployment (VPC) with the Redwood Private control plane. Control plane in us-west; inference plane in customer VPC via peered subnet.
- Dedicated GPU pool for steady state (2 x A100-80GB equiv per shard, 3 shards) to cover sustained 150 RPS at 2048 context with 13B quantized performance.
- Burst capacity via dedicated autoscale group (spot or reserved burst nodes) that can add 8 x 80GB-equivalent GPUs for short windows — target spin-up < 90s.
- Overflow routing: when autoscale cannot catch up, route to a quantized 7B variant (lower memory, faster p95) with automated fallbacks at 75% CPU/GPU saturation.

Latency & batching guidance:
- For interactive short responses (<=64 tokens) target batching windows of 6–12ms with dynamic batching up to 64 tokens to maximize throughput while keeping p95 < 400ms.
- KV cache policy: persistent per-session prefix caching; expect ~40–60% cache hit — reduces compute by ~30% on multi-turn flows.
- Kernel selection: we'll recommend FP16/4-bit quantization profile (we tested a 4-bit Q4_K_M profile on 13B with ~2–2.5x memory reduction, performance within 7–10% quality delta).

Cost & capacity estimate (very rough):
- Steady state (150 RPS): 3 shards on 80GB-equivalent gives headroom for 1.2x traffic and maintenance overhead.
- Peak (700 RPS burst): autoscale to +8 GPUs, plus fallback to 7B for ~30% of requests reduces effective cost during peak by ~45% vs scaling only 13B.

Security/compliance notes:
- KMS integration supported; we can ingest your key policy and validate HSM flow or customer-managed keys.
- We will provide SOC2 and audit-log sample (Irene — attaching a short excerpt to this thread).

Proposed next steps & timeline:
1) Redwood to produce a short topology diagram + capacity table (by Fri Oct 11) — includes exact GPU counts, expected p95 under test harness.
2) OpsAI to share sample logs (redacted) and the SOC/security questionnaire sections they prioritize (by Mon Oct 14).
3) Schedule a 45-min demo + live latency run (week of Oct 14).

Attachments: OpsAI-MAP.pdf (Mutual Action Plan draft) — I attached a first-pass MAP and the throughput matrix back to your Drive.

Action owners:
- Markus: MAP + topology diagram (deliver Fri Oct 11)
- Irene: SOC2/audit-log excerpt + KMS integration notes (deliver Thu Oct 10)
- Grace: Perf validation plan and benchmark script for 13B/7B comparison (deliver Mon Oct 14)

If this reads true to your expectations I’ll schedule the demo and block time for a live run.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Sun <claire.sun@opsai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi@opsai.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Oct 2029 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OpsAI discovery recap — throughput & latency constraints

Markus / team — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. Quick notes and asks: 

1) Prioritization: p95 <= 400ms for <=64 token responses is our top SLA ask for the interactive product; everything else is second priority.
2) Procurement window: we're targeting a signed contract and deployment window by Nov 22.
3) Security: I attached the SOC sections we prioritize to the Drive folder (see link). Can you confirm if Dedicated burst nodes can be reserved as On-Demand for guaranteed spin-up?

Also please send a DocuSign for the MAP when you have the version with committed delivery dates — procurement will need that to start the purchase order.

On the demo: Ravi and I are available Oct 15 or Oct 16 (AM PT). Either day works — prefer an early slot.

Thanks — Claire

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Internal: OpsAI next steps & owner assignment

Irene / Grace — copying Claire for visibility but primarily assigning internal tasks. Quick internal checklist post-call:

Irene:
- Send SOC2 excerpt and audit-log sample into the Drive folder (Thu Oct 10). Include KMS HSM integration notes and a short section on retained metadata.
- Confirm whether we can expose a per-customer KMS flow for Private deploy — if not, list work needed and ETA.

Grace:
- Prepare perf harness and run a 13B Q4_K_M profile vs 7B quantized baseline. Deliver initial numbers (p50/p95 for 64 tokens) by Mon Oct 14. Include the benchmark script in the shared Drive.

Markus:
- Finalize topology diagram and MAP with dates by Fri Oct 11; prepare a DocuSign-ready MAP for OpsAI procurement.

Claire — we’ll confirm the Oct 15 morning slot once Grace confirms availability. Will try to make the live run show both 13B and 7B fallbacks under a simulated campaign burst.

Thanks — on it.

Markus
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference
